html:
The Karakum Canal is one of the longest irrigation canals in the world. It takes water from the Amu Darya river and carries it west for some 1,375 kilometres across the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan.

Work began in 1954. The first section opened in 1958; the canal reached Ashgabat in the early 1960s and was extended in stages toward the Caspian into the 1980s. Much of it is navigable.

It turned large stretches of desert into cotton fields and made modern Turkmenistan possible: most of its farming and its towns depend on it. But it is an open, unlined ditch through sand, and a large part of the water seeps away or evaporates before it arrives. The canal takes a big share of the Amu Darya's flow, and it is one of the main reasons the Aral Sea shrank. It was the largest of a family of Soviet water projects that began with the Great Fergana Canal.
sum: The Karakum Canal is one of the longest irrigation canals in the world. It takes water from the Amu Darya river and carries it west for some 1,375 kilometres across the Karakum Desert of Turkmenistan.
